9.0.s.en: 1. A light that shone in the darkness:

9.0.0.en: 1 But there shall be no gloom for her that was in anguish. As in the former time he humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, so in the latter he honors the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the nations. 2 The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined. 3 Thou hast multiplied the nation, thou hast magnified the joy for it: they joy before thee according to the joy in harvest, and as men rejoice when they divide the spoil. 4 For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, thou hast broken as in the day of Midian. 5 For every weapon of the armed man in the battle, and every garment rolled in blood, shall be for burning, fuel of fire.

9.0.1.en: The end of the previous chapter was extremely dark, so this chapter begins with the word “But”... for God does not leave His people like this, but wants to shine upon them with His light.

9.0.2.en: “But there shall be no gloom for her that was in anguish. As in the former time he humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, so in the latter he honors the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the nations. The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined” [1-2]. This prophecy was fulfilled by the appearing of the Lord Christ and His preaching in Galilee of the nations. The Evangelist says: “That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles; The people which sat in darkness saw great light” (Mt 4:14-16). This region was marked by lowliness, so Nathanael says: “Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?” (Jn 1:46). Perhaps this is because this spot (Galilee of the nations) lies on the border of the nations, so it was exposed to invasions, and because of its mixing with the neighboring pagan nations it took on many pagan customs and remained for long periods in spiritual decay; therefore the prophet put it: “The people that sat in darkness.”

9.0.3.en: The region of Galilee was a district comprising twenty cities which Solomon gave to Hiram king of Tyre. The Jews in it were few in number; most of its inhabitants were Phoenicians, Greeks and Arabs, therefore it was called “Galilee of the nations.” The Lord Christ, the Teacher of mankind and the Sun of Righteousness, came to it to shine upon those who sit in darkness. As for the district of Capernaum, whose name means “Comforter,” it is considered one of the most important districts of Galilee; it was a Roman fortress in which there was a garrison of Roman commanders.

9.0.4.en: * He dwelt in Galilee so that those who sit in darkness might see a great light.

9.0.5.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * Let those who sit in the darkness of ignorance see the great light of perfect knowledge; the old things are passed away, behold, all things are become new (2 Cor 5:17); the letter has ended and the Spirit has advanced, the shadows have fled and the truth has come to them.

9.0.6.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * By faith they come out of the darkness and death of sin into light and life.

9.0.7.en: St. Augustine * The light of the Logos, who is life, shines in the darkness of our souls; He comes to where the rulers of this darkness are, who oppose the human race to subject it to darkness. These rulers do not stand firm in their power when the light shines upon them, which came to make human beings children of light.

9.0.8.en: Origen God does not allow the darkness to last, but shines with His light... So what happens?

9.1.0.en: a. “Thou hast multiplied the nation” [3]; although it fell under discipline with severe blows, it grows and multiplies by the mercy and grace of God.

9.1.1.en: b. “Thou hast magnified the joy” [3]. The nation rejoices as on the day of harvest or the day of enjoying the spoil, as though the secret of its joy were the abundant harvest and the triumph or victory over the enemy of good.

9.1.2.en: Joy is the mark of the Church of the New Testament, rejoicing in the Gospel life in the midst of sufferings. She rejoices over her continual harvest of many souls for the sake of the Kingdom of God, and enjoys the spoil of victory over the enemy of good. Her life is continual rejoicing over the souls that repent and enjoy salvation and over her unceasing victories.

9.2.0.en: c. Enjoying glorious freedom: “For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, thou hast broken as in the day of Midian” [4]. She is freed from the heavy yoke and the staff and the rod of forced labor, as a symbol of freedom and salvation from the slavery of the devil through the Cross, so that the devil and his powers no longer have authority over the believer who enjoys the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

9.3.0.en: 6 For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace. 7 Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will perform this.

9.3.1.en: The secret of the nation's enjoyment of continual growth and lasting joy together with glorious freedom is the coming of the Messiah as Savior, Conqueror and Victor on behalf of mankind against the enemies. The Son of God came incarnate to bear the yoke of the Cross in our name, and so He gives us every possibility of salvation. For the prophet says: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given, and the government shall be upon his shoulder, and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, for the increase of his government, and of peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will perform this” [6-7].

9.3.2.en: Believing mankind was awaiting the divine Incarnation, in which the Son of God, who is the Creator, the Giver of life and its glory, comes to raise our dead and corrupted nature to the goodness in which it was created, by re-creating it and renewing it continually, so that He gives it continuity of life together with joy and freedom.

9.3.3.en: a. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given,” that is, He becomes man, so that the Son of God becomes the Son of Man and is reckoned a child, bearing our human nature truly in the perfection of its form, without separation from His divinity and without mingling or confusion or alteration. He shares our human life except for sin and remains as He is, “the Son of God”... The Apostle says: “Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil” (Heb 3:14).

9.3.4.en: * He became man in the body of our salvation, so that He might have something to offer on our behalf as salvation for us all.

9.3.5.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic * Who is this who wants us to share in His flesh and blood? Surely He is the Son of God! How did He become a partner with us except through flesh? And how did He break the bonds of death except by His bodily death? For Christ's endurance of death put death to death.

9.3.6.en: St. Ambrose b. “And the government shall be upon his shoulder,” for He reigned from a tree, as the Psalmist says, the tree of the Cross which He carried on His shoulder as the throne of His divine love.

9.3.7.en: * The government shall be upon his shoulder, for He entered His Kingdom by carrying the Cross.

9.3.8.en: Origen * This means the power of the Cross, because He used His shoulders when He was crucified, by carrying the Cross.

9.3.9.en: The martyr Justin c. “His name shall be called Wonderful,” because He is beyond comprehension; He was given a name which is above every name, that at his name every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth (Phil 2:9-11).

9.3.10.en: The disciples and apostles realized the power of the name “Jesus”; by it they preached, and by it they healed the sick, cast out demons and raised the dead.

9.3.11.en: The writings of Origen reveal the early Church's esteem for the name of Jesus as a secret of power to which the believer holds fast in order to live as a conqueror and victor over sin and Satan and all the powers of darkness. Among his words: [By His name demons are often driven out of people, especially if it is repeated in a sound manner and with full confidence. Great is the name of Jesus, which has its effectiveness even if the wicked sometimes use it. The name of Jesus heals those who suffer in mind, and drives out the spirits of darkness, and grants healing to the sick.] He also declares that His titles reveal His manifold and abounding grace, for he says: [Although Christ is one in His essence, He has many titles that point to His authority and His works; it is understood that He is grace, righteousness, peace, life, truth, the Word...]

9.3.12.en: d. “Counsellor,” as He is “the wisdom of God” (1 Cor 1:24), in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (1 Cor 2:3). The Septuagint reads “the Messenger of the great counsel”... What is this great counsel for which the Father sent Him? The revelation of the divine mystery to mankind, and the disclosure of the Father, whom no one knows except the Son and he to whom the Son will reveal Him.

9.3.13.en: * The Son of God was called thus (the Messenger of the great counsel) because of the things He taught, especially because He revealed the Father to mankind, for He says: “I have manifested thy name unto the men” (Jn 17:6)... He declared His name by words and deeds.

9.3.14.en: St. John Chrysostom * There is no knowledge without faith, and no faith without knowledge... The Son is the true Teacher about the Father; we believe in the Son in order to know the Father, with whom also is the Son. Again, in order to know the Father we must believe in the Son, for He is the Son of the Father. The knowledge of the Father and the Son, in the manner of the true Gnostic, is the attainment of the truth by means of the truth... Truly, few are those who believe and know.

9.3.15.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * The divine Word was sent as a physician to sinners, and as a teacher of the divine mysteries to those who are pure and without sin.

9.3.16.en: Origen e. “The mighty God”: true God of true God, one with the Father in essence, who alone is able to renew our nature as the Creator, and the Intercessor who alone is able to atone for the sins of the whole world.

9.3.17.en: f. “The everlasting Father”: He attaches the title “Mighty God” to “Everlasting Father,” to declare that the power of the Lord Christ, the true God, is not in displaying might and greatness but rather in offering a unique fatherhood of love toward mankind, through which we enjoy the power of Christ in us. He is the almighty Creator who gives Himself to His believers as members of His body and as His children, so that they bear His capacities within them. In other words, in Christ Jesus the incomprehensible power of God is revealed together with His surpassing practical love, so that we may say with the Apostle: “I can do all things through Christ Jesus who strengtheneth me.”

9.3.18.en: g. “The Prince of Peace”: He is the King of Peace (1 Thess 5:23), who offers us His blood for our reconciliation with the Father, so that we carry inner peace with Him (Rom 5:1), peace with God and with ourselves and with our brethren, shattering the wall of enmity, inward and outward.

9.4.0.en: He is the Son of David, “Prince and King,” not on the level of earth and time, but to reign eternally upon the throne of His father David (Lk 1:32-33) on the level of the inner heart and eternity; neither His kingdom nor His peace has any limits [7].

9.4.1.en: He reigns with truth and righteousness, as He hides us in Himself so that we become walkers in the truth, bearing His righteousness. The cause of this is that “the zeal of the LORD of hosts will perform this”; He is zealous over mankind as the heavenly Bridegroom united with His bride.

9.4.2.en: In brief, the prophet Isaiah declares this wondrous, mighty Child, who does not save Ahaz from the opposition of his enemies, but establishes a new kingdom whose foundation is the throne of David, a kingdom of true peace that extends to the peoples and nations, and of whose peace there is no end [7], as He gives us Himself, the mystery of eternal peace.

9.4.3.en: * Behold, the Son of God has been given to us.

9.4.4.en: A little later he says: “And of peace there shall be no end” [7].

9.4.5.en: The Romans have limits (an end), but the kingdom of the Son of God is without limits.

9.4.6.en: Persia and Media have limits, but the Son has no limits.

9.4.7.en: He says after that: “Upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom...”; the holy Virgin is of the seed of David.

9.5.0.en: 8 The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. 9 And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria, that say in the pride and stoutness of heart, 10 “The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones: the sycomores are cut down, but we will change them into cedars.” 11 Therefore the LORD shall set up the adversaries of Rezin against him, and join his enemies together; 12 The Syrians before, and the Philistines behind; and they shall devour Israel with open mouth. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

9.5.1.en: The Word of God, in His unlimited love, condescends to become man in order to give light to those who sit in darkness, shining upon them with His divine light, granting them the light of knowledge, offering them His life as the mystery of joy and rejoicing and continual victory; but man, on the contrary, exalts himself in pride, reckoning in himself that he is able by his human arm to accomplish salvation. This is what happened in the days of the prophet Isaiah and what happens through the ages; the house of Jacob exalted themselves, rejecting his prophetic counsel, and also in the days of the Lord Christ when they denied faith in Him... Yet with all this, the hand of God remains stretched out in love, awaiting man's return to Him.

9.5.2.en: In this passage there are three poetic verses in Hebrew that end with the phrase: “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still” [12, 17, 20] [also (Isa 10:4)].

9.5.3.en: Some see that this outstretched divine hand is a sign of God's calling to man to draw near to Him and meet with Him and be united with Him. It is also a sign of God's protection of him, as though He were assuring him that however great the obstacles, the hand of the Almighty is stretched out to save him from every evil and rescue him from bitterness and distress. It is also a sign of the divine discipline springing from love, He stretches out His hand to press upon man so that he returns to himself and seeks God as his helper. These three signs were fulfilled through the Incarnation of the Word, in which He calls us to sonship to God, offers us free salvation, and bears the wages of sin in His body to draw us to Himself. The divine hand is a symbol of the divine Word, who came down to us to declare the love of the Father and to reconcile us with Him by His blood as the price of our sins and transgressions.

9.6.0.en: God, in His love, allowed distress for the kingdom of Israel (Ephraim), but instead of repenting they exalted themselves all the more. This is what the prophet revealed by saying: “That say in the pride and stoutness of heart, The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones: the sycomores are cut down, but we will change them into cedars” [10]. Some see that the prophet is speaking here about the earthquake that occurred in the days of Uzziah, which seems to have been widespread (Amos 1:1; Zech 14:5); because of it most of the houses of Samaria and Ephraim fell and there were many victims, and they began to mock the judgment of God, declaring that although He had permitted the destruction of their houses made of brick and the fall of the sycamore trees, they would erect palaces made of hewn stones and plant cedar trees that an earthquake could neither demolish nor remove. It is as though in this they repeat what man did when he set out to build the tower of Babel so that its top might reach to heaven (Gen 11:3-4).

9.7.0.en: The prophet Isaiah answers this by announcing a more severe chastening from God: since they did not tremble at the earthquake, He will allow the enemy “Rezin,” king of Syria, to rage, and He also stirs up his enemies (perhaps he meant Assyria, which attacked Israel and afterward turned against Judah). He allows the nations to rage against Israel to devour them completely, as a beast devours sheep and swallows them: “And they shall devour Israel with open mouth” [12]; yet the mercies of God remain awaiting their return, as he continues his speech: “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still” [12].

9.8.0.en: 13 For the people turneth not unto him that smiteth them, neither do they seek the LORD of hosts. 14 Therefore the LORD will cut off from Israel head and tail, branch and rush, in one day. 15 The ancient and honourable, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail. 16 For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed. 17 Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men, neither shall have mercy on their fatherless and widows: for every one is an hypocrite and an evildoer, and every mouth speaketh folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. 18 For wickedness burneth as the fire: it shall devour the briers and thorns, and shall kindle in the thickets of the forest, and they shall mount up like the lifting up of smoke. 19 Through the wrath of the LORD of hosts is the land burned up, and the people shall be as the fuel of the fire: no man shall spare his brother. 20 And he shall snatch on the right hand, and be hungry; and he shall eat on the left hand, and they shall not be satisfied: they shall eat every man the flesh of his own arm: 21 Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh: and they together shall be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

9.9.0.en: The people remain hard of heart, therefore: “The LORD will cut off from Israel head and tail, branch and rush (halfa grass or straw), in one day” [14].

9.9.1.en: a. He removes the leaders of the people, whatever their rank (the head, the branch).

9.9.2.en: b. He removes the false prophets (the tail, the rush).

9.10.0.en: c. The destruction of the guides because they cause them to err [16].

9.11.0.en: d. He takes no pleasure in the young men because of their youth, nor in the orphans or the widows, although He is “a father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows” (Ps 68:5)... for all together shared in evil, with stubbornness and arrogance and folly [17]. The Assyrian kings were extremely cruel: Tiglath-pileser showed no mercy to the young, or to the widows or orphans in Ephraim.

9.12.0.en: e. The whole people turn into something like a forest burning with the fire of divine wrath [19], not because God takes vengeance for Himself, but because their wickedness is a destroying fire [18].

9.12.1.en: f. The nation turns into a state of chaos whose law is violence and injustice and insatiability, ruled by bloody, destructive civil wars: “No man shall spare his brother. He shall snatch on the right hand, and be hungry; and he shall eat on the left hand, and they shall not be satisfied: they shall eat every man the flesh of his own arm (that is, his neighbor or relative)” [19-20]... This is a hideous picture of a society whose law is war, violence and selfishness with greed. One consumes the other (Gal 5:15), and as the prophet Haggai says: “Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes” (Hag 1:6), a sign that their life is empty of the blessing of the Lord and His grace.

9.13.0.en: g. The infighting does not stop at individuals but creeps into the tribes themselves, so that one tribe allies with another against a third, and so on: “Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh: and they together shall be against Judah” [21].

9.13.1.en: “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still” [21].
